title: Climbing a Sand Dune
hook: What if you climb a sand dune?

beats.label: 10 MINUTES
beats.line: After ten minutes, your skin starts to glisten with sweat.
beats.idea: Close‑up of the character’s forehead, sweat beads forming.

beats.label: 30 MINUTES
beats.line: By half an hour, you feel your heart thumping faster.
beats.idea: Animated heart icon beating faster, pulse line on forearm.

beats.label: 1 HOUR
beats.line: After an hour, your mouth dries and you crave water.
beats.idea: Character licking dry lips, a water bottle nearby.

beats.label: 3 HOURS
beats.line: By three hours, your shoulders turn pink from sunburn.

beats.label: 6 HOURS
beats.line: Six hours in, sand gets into your eyes, they water.
beats.idea: Character blinking, sand particles floating, tears streaming.

description: A paper‑craft explorer climbs a dune while we see the real physiological changes from heat and effort.

facts.claim: Sweating begins within minutes of moderate exercise in hot conditions.
Heart rate increases to meet higher oxygen demand during exertion.
Dehydration causes dry mouth and thirst after about an hour of vigorous activity without fluid intake.
UV exposure can cause sunburn after 30 minutes of direct sunlight on exposed skin.
Windblown sand can irritate eyes, causing tearing and discomfort.

end.line: Would you keep climbing under the desert sun?

topic: What happens if you climb a sand dune?
